title: Abundance of Fungal Hyphae in Seawater by Epifluorescence Microscopy
author: M.H. Gutiérrez

steps.title: Collect and fix seawater samples
steps.instruction: Collect seawater in sterile 50 mL polypropylene tubes, add formaldehyde or glutaraldehyde to reach a final concentration of 2 % (v/v), mix, and store the tubes at 4 °C in the dark until further processing.

steps.title: Filter appropriate volume onto filters
steps.instruction: Filter 5 mL–30 mL (depending on the environment) of the fixed seawater through a 0.22 µm black polycarbonate filter (25 mm diameter, Millipore Corp.) using vacuum filtration; retain the filter with the captured material.

steps.title: Stain retained material with Calcofluor
steps.instruction: Apply 600 µL of aqueous 0.1 % Calcofluor White directly onto the filter, ensuring the entire filter area is covered; incubate for 5–10 minutes in darkness; then use vacuum to remove excess stain while avoiding any light exposure.

substeps.instruction: Apply 600 µL 0.1 % Calcofluor White to filter
Vacuum‑remove excess stain, keep away from light

steps.title: Mount filter on microscope slide
steps.instruction: Place the filter sample‑side up on a clean microscope slide, add one drop of non‑fluorescent immersion oil on top of the filter, and gently cover with a cover slip.

steps.title: Prepare slides for microscopy
steps.instruction: Either examine the slide immediately on an epifluorescence microscope or, if analysis will be delayed, store the slide at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Observe and count hyphae
steps.instruction: Using an epifluorescence microscope equipped with a UV DAPI filter set 49 (Zeiss; 365 nm excitation, 445–450 nm emission) at 1000× magnification, scan the entire effective area of the filter, count all hyphae, and record each filament’s length and width.

steps.title: Calculate biovolume and estimate biomass
steps.instruction: Model each hypha as a cylinder using the recorded length and width to calculate biovolume; estimate fungal biomass from biovolume using the biovolume‑to‑biomass ratios reported by Newell and Statzell‑Tallman (1982).
